digest.en: Jensen Huang’s return locks Nvidia deeper into US statecraft, reshaping semiconductor policy. Meanwhile, the UN warns the Gaza war has undone 77 years of human development. These threads highlight the widening gap between geopolitical strategy and human cost.
digest.hi: चीन के स्पेस स्टेशन में पाकिस्तानी एस्ट्रोनॉट की पहली विदेशी यात्रा की तैयारी अमेरिका में ट्रंप और जेन्सेन की संपत्ति संबंधी खबरों के बीच चल रही है। यूएई में बस-ट्रक हादसे में 11 मौतों के बाद क्षेत्रीय सुरक्षा और स्वास्थ्य संकटों का दायरा और फैल गया है।

articles.title: Contrer la menace du Jnim sur les centres urbains du Sahel
articles.summary: Al-Qaeda in the Sahel has intensified attacks on urban centers. Military responses risk worsening the human toll. Negotiated solutions may offer a less damaging path forward for the region. Ces dernières années, la branche d’al-Qaeda au Sahel a multiplié les assauts contre les villes de la région. Chercher à vaincre les jihadistes par les armes ne ferait qu’alourdir un bilan humain déjà considérable.

articles.title: Questions sur un retour en force
articles.summary: Crisis Group analysts discussed the deployment of Algerian troops in Niger. They examined how this military presence affects regional security balances. The conversation highlighted shifting dynamics in the Sahel. Dans cet épisode d’Afrique 360°, Enrica Picco et Rinaldo Depagne reçoivent Ibrahim Yahaya Ibrahim, Directeur Adjoint du Projet Sahel, Ibrahim Maïga, Conseiller Spécial pour le Sahel et Michaël Ayari, Analyste Senior pour la Tunisie et l’Algérie à Crisis Group, pour parler du déploiement de troupes algériennes au Niger et des répercussions de cette présence militaire sur les équilibres sécuritaires.

articles.title: Huang’s comeback won’t ease Southeast Asia’s data center crunch
articles.summary: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia chief executive after a board vote. Nvidia shares rose over 31 percent in New York. Southeast Asia still faces a severe data center shortage despite the stock rally. Monday’s unanimous board vote reinstating Jensen Huang as Nvidia chief executive, backed publicly by US President Donald Trump, triggered a sharp relief rally across global artificial intelligence stocks, with Nvidia shares surging more than 31% in New York trading.

articles.title: Coating wear makes China’s stealth fighters easier to target
articles.summary: New data shows stealth coating wear increases radar reflection. Losing ten percent of the coating nearly doubles microwave power. This challenges the effectiveness of low-observable aircraft in harsh conditions. New laboratory data on stealth coating degradation, rapidly expanding fighter fleets, harsh maritime sustainment, and evolving counter-stealth sensors test whether low-observable aircraft can stay decisive without broader operational adaptation. This month, the South China Morning Post (SCMP) reported that losing just 10% of a radar-absorbing coating can nearly double reflected microwave power in.

articles.title: How Herat defied the Taliban regime, chanting ‘women, work and freedom’
articles.summary: Women in Herat protested Taliban dress code enforcement in early June. Authorities arrested many women for wearing traditional manto instead of burqa. Communities rallied, leading to the release of the detainees. The protests in the Afghan city in the first week of June were triggered by the enforcement of a dress code, which requires women to wear burqa in public; many women, including those wearing traditional Afghan wear of manto, were arrested, but released later as entire communities protested.

articles.title: Asia rescues markets, Trump rescues Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Asian governments banned short sales and deployed state funds to stabilize markets after a global selloff hit the artificial intelligence sector. Seoul, Taipei, and Beijing acted to prevent a tech rout from spreading. Trump also intervened to support Jensen Huang during the downturn. NEW YORK – When a brutal global selloff wiped trillions of dollars off the artificial intelligence trade, Asia’s policymakers did what they always do: they reached deep into their crisis playbooks.

articles.title: Barbados town’s three-year deal with Bristol ‘part of the reparative process’
articles.summary: Speightstown in Barbados signed a three-year twinning agreement with Bristol, United Kingdom. Labour minister Colin Jordan stated the deal acknowledges the historical links between the two places. The partnership is described as part of a broader reparative process regarding the transatlantic slave trade. Island’s labour minister, Colin Jordan, says agreement acknowledges links between Speightstown and UK city are rooted in slave tradeA town in Barbados known as “Little Bristol” has signed a “twinning’” agreement with the UK city, marking a new chapter in a centuries-long relationship rooted in the transatlantic slave trade. Barbados says the new partnership between Speightstown and Bristol is part.

articles.title: Jensen Huang’s return locks Nvidia deeper into US statecraft
articles.summary: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO less than two weeks after his resignation. Shares surged roughly thirty percent in New York trading. Investors priced in product roadmap continuity, treating the reversal as an immediate restoration of the status quo. When Nvidia’s board voted unanimously on Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive less than two weeks after his resignation, equity markets treated the reversal as an immediate restoration of the status quo.

articles.title: Gaza war has undone 77 years of human development, UN warns
articles.summary: The UN deputy chief warned that the Gaza war has undone seventy-seven years of human development. Palestinians face violence and displacement despite the October 2025 ceasefire. He urged renewed international support for a two-state solution to the conflict. The UN deputy chief urged renewed international support for a two-State solution to the Israel-Palestine conflict on Monday, warning that Palestinians continue to face violence, displacement and dire living conditions despite the October 2025 ceasefire in Gaza.

articles.title: UN chief urges talks on global AI safety framework, warns of historic shift in power
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for talks on a multilateral AI safety framework. He warned that artificial intelligence is driving the biggest transfer of power in human history. Member States must begin discussions to manage these emerging technological risks. UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Monday called on Member States to begin discussions on a multilateral framework for managing the risks of artificial intelligence (AI), warning that the technology is driving “the biggest transfer of power in the history of humankind”.

articles.title: Ukraine Strikes Russian Warship, Cargo Vessel Off Libya's Coast
articles.summary: Ukraine struck a Russian corvette and a cargo ship near Benghazi, Libya. Seven Ukrainian-made sea drones executed the operation. The corvette carried a Ka-27 helicopter. The cargo vessel allegedly transported weapons across the Mediterranean Sea. Kyiv confirmed the details of the attack. Ukraine says that it struck a Russian corvette carrying a Ka-27 helicopter near the port of Benghazi, Libya, as well as a cargo ship allegedly used to transport weapons across the Mediterranean Sea.

articles.title: Why Taiwanese firms resist leaving China, even as tensions rise
articles.summary: Acer and Asus are relocating production lines from Thailand and Vietnam back to mainland China. The move counters rising geopolitical tensions and leverages established supply chains. Stan Shih represented Taiwan at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. The shift highlights the economic pull of the Chinese market despite political friction. When Stan Shih, the founder of electronics company Acer, arrived in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen to represent Taiwan at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit recently, his company was already in the news.

articles.title: SE Asia’s AI collision: when CAFTA 3.0 hits the US cloud clock
articles.summary: The China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 upgrade enters into force next month. Leaders confirmed the protocol in Manila on November 16. The pact extends beyond tariffs to include digital trade and AI standards. It also covers e-payments and smart customs single windows. In Manila on November 16, Chinese and ASEAN leaders confirmed that the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area (CAFTA) 3.0 upgrade protocol will formally enter into force at the start of next month.

articles.title: At least 24 killed and dozens missing in confectionery factory fire in Indonesia
articles.summary: At least 24 people died in a fire at a confectionery factory in Indonesia. Rescuers searched unstable structures for about 30 missing workers. Authorities are investigating the cause of the blaze that broke out on Saturday. DNA testing is required to identify the victims. Rescuers brave unstable structures in search for missing as DNA needed to identify victimsIndonesia has confirmed the deaths of 24 people in a fire that tore ⁠through a factory, as rescuers braved unstable structures in the burned wreckage to search for ⁠about 30 people ⁠still missing. Authorities ​were still investigating the cause of the fire, which broke out on Saturday in the PT Fonusa Agung Mu.

articles.title: China’s plan to weaponize infrastructure gear
articles.summary: China imposed strict export controls on tunnel boring machines on November 18. The move coincided with the APEC summit. Leaders from Indonesia, Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand stayed in the region. They skipped their flights home to discuss the new restrictions. On November 18, the day APEC leaders gathered, China quietly activated a powerful new geopolitical weapon: strict export controls on tunnel boring machines (TBMs).

articles.title: NATO-Like Guarantees For Ukraine? US Envoy Signals Possibility, But Questions Remain
articles.summary: Jared Kushner said Donald Trump might offer Ukraine security guarantees modeled on NATO commitments. This possibility hinges on reducing the risk of another Russian invasion. The envoy signaled this potential shift on November 22. Questions remain regarding the specific terms and conditions of such an arrangement. US President Donald Trump may consider offering Ukraine security guarantees modeled on NATO's collective-defense commitments if he is convinced that the risk of another Russian invasion has been sufficiently reduced, special envoy Jared Kushner said on November 22.

articles.title: Rescuers Search For Victims After Russia Attacks Apartment Building Near Kyiv
articles.summary: Russian drones destroyed a residential building in Dymer, 45 kilometers north of Kyiv. At least five people died, including an 18-year-old man. Rescuers searched for survivors and other victims. The attack targeted a civilian area near the capital. At least five people were confirmed dead after Russian drone strikes destroyed a residential building in the town of Dymer, about 45 kilometers north of Kyiv.

articles.title: COP31 ends without climate pact as UN chief warns there is ‘no ambiguity in the science’
articles.summary: COP31 concluded without a binding climate agreement. Negotiators failed to resolve disputes over fossil fuel phaseouts. UN Secretary-General António Guterres called the outcome deeply disappointing. The two-week summit ended with no new commitments to accelerate global emissions reductions. COP31 ended on Sunday without a climate pact after negotiators failed to overcome divisions over fossil fuels, bringing two weeks of talks and two days of overtime to a close that UN Secretary-General António Guterres described as a “deeply disappointing” setback.

articles.title: ‘I had a better life in Iran’: Afghan women forced home struggle to rebuild
articles.summary: Afghan women returning from Iran face unemployment and fractured families. Zahra, a midwife in Herat, lost her income and now lives with her parents. Her son remains with her ex-husband. The five-year displacement left her without a stable livelihood or support network in her home region. For five years, Zahra cared for an elderly woman in Iran and earned enough to get by.

articles.title: Guterres laments COP31 outcome, urges climate justice from Barbados
articles.summary: António Guterres expressed disappointment over the collapse of COP31 negotiations. He made the comments during a visit to Barbados. The Secretary-General urged stronger action on fossil fuels. He also called for increased climate finance for vulnerable nations. Secretary-General António Guterres on Sunday expressed deep disappointment over the collapse of COP31 climate negotiations, using a visit to Barbados to call for stronger action on fossil fuels, climate finance and support for vulnerable nations.

articles.title: Afghan Women Turn To Social Media To Earn Living As Doors Close Offline
articles.summary: Afghan women are building personal brands on social media. They use Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube to earn a living. Content features cooking, shopping, and family gatherings. This shift occurs as offline opportunities have closed under Taliban rule. Afghan women who have had their lives sharply restricted by Taliban rule have responded by building personal brands on Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube showing them cooking at home, shopping in bazaars, or meeting friends and family.

articles.title: Iran To Ration Electricity Amid Warnings Power Grid Battered by US, Israeli Strikes
articles.summary: Iran will begin rationing electricity on November 22. This follows recent bread shortages and purchase management procedures. The move occurs as uncertainty grows over President Trump’s next diplomatic or military step. The government aims to manage domestic resource scarcity. Iran To Ration Electricity As World Awaits Trump's Next Move. Iran To Ration Electricity Amid Warnings Power Grid Battered by US, Israeli Strikes.

articles.title: ‘We escaped with only our lives’: Fighting to give birth in war-torn Yemen
articles.summary: Midwife Anisa Fadhl fled Taiz, Yemen, as fighting escalated two months ago. She left without packing a bag. Her home and clinic were later looted and destroyed. She escaped with only her life. The conflict displaced many medical workers. When fighting suddenly escalated around Taiz, in southwestern Yemen two months ago, midwife Anisa Fadhl had no time to pack a bag before she fled, leaving behind her home and her clinic.

articles.title: High Stakes in Iraq’s Push to Reclaim Jurf al-Sakhar
articles.summary: Iraqi government forces entered Jurf al-Sakhar on 20 November to reclaim the area from Kata’ib Hizbollah. Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi restored state authority in the stronghold. Crisis Group expert Lahib Higel explained the circumstances that allowed the military operation to proceed successfully. On 20 November, Iraqi government forces entered Jurf al-Sakhar, a stronghold of the Iran-backed group Kata’ib Hizbollah. In this Q&A, Crisis Group expert Lahib Higel explains the circumstances that allowed Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi to restore state authority in this area.

articles.title: General Assembly President tells Rohingya refugees after genocide ruling
articles.summary: The President of the UN General Assembly visited Cox’s Bazar refugee camps in Bangladesh. This occurred one day after the International Court of Justice ruled Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. The official urged the international community to turn the landmark judgement into concrete action. A day after the UN’s highest court found that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya, the President of the General Assembly visited the refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, urging the world to turn the landmark judgement into action.

articles.summary: अमेरिका ने 26 साल बाद खसरे से मुक्त होने का दर्जा खो दिया है। बीमारी 12 महीने से फैल रही है। वर्जीनिया और पेंसिल्वेनिया में 13 मौतें हुईं। बच्चों और वयस्कों दोनों को खतरा है। बांग्लादेश में खसरे ने 1,350 से ज्यादा लोगों की जान ले ली है. वहां टीकों की कमी से हालात बिगड़े हैं. अब यही खतरनाक बीमारी 26 साल बाद अमेरिका में भी लौट आई है.

articles.summary: बेनाम ट्रॉपिकल तूफान ने फ्लोरिडा में 5 से 20 इंच बारिश कराई। कई इलाके डूब गए। सेंट जॉन्स नदी का पानी बढ़ा। मिड-अटलांटिक क्षेत्र बुरे असर से बच गया। उत्तर की ओर बढ़ने से पहले ही नुकसान हुआ। एक बेनाम ट्रॉपिकल हवाओं और बारिश वाले तूफान के चलते कई इलाकों में तेज हवाओं, ऊंची समुद्री लहरों और मूसलाधार बारिश से सड़कों व हाईवे पर जलभराव का खतरा बना हुआ है, हालांकि सिस्टम के देर से मजबूत होने के कारण मिड-अटलांटिक क्षेत्र सबसे बुरे असर से बच गया.

articles.summary: अमेरिका ने ईरान पर आर्थिक दबाव बढ़ाने के लिए नया कदम उठाया है। शैडो बैंकिंग नेटवर्कों पर प्रतिबंध लगाए गए हैं। दोनों देशों के बीच तनाव जारी है। ईरान (Iran) और अमेरिका (United States of America) के बीच तनाव की स्थिति पहले जैसे ही बनी हुई है। एक-दूसरे की शर्तों पर सहमति नहीं बन पाने की वजह से दोनों देशों के बीच कोई समझौता नहीं हो रहा है।
